lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: At sixty three, I ran into my ex-husband in Walmart. He was with her. The woman he left me for. She is forty one.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Michelle? Is that you? My God, what happened, did you get work done? You look so much more beautiful.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: It is just me.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: The only reason I did not fall apart standing there is because of what my sister handed me a few weeks ago.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: I am sorry, Michelle. After thirty one years. I just... I need something different.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: Thirty one years.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: When did I start looking like this? Tired. Worn out. Older than I am. No wonder he stopped looking at me.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: I stopped looking in mirrors. I stopped being in photos. And I buried my face under more and more makeup that only made it worse.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: Every cream. Every serum. Every foundation on the shelf. The Estée Lauder, the L’Oréal. And I look older in all of them.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: I decided this was just what sixty looked like, and I made my peace with disappearing.

lines.speaker: ROSA
lines.text: Michelle, open the door. I brought wine and I am not leaving. ...Oh, honey. Look at you. Come here.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: I am fine, Rosa. I am. I just... I do not know who that woman in the mirror is anymore. He looked at me like a stranger the day he left, and lately so do I.

lines.speaker: ROSA
lines.text: Can I tell you something? Two years ago, I felt exactly like that. Same mirror, same thoughts. And I will tell you what I had to learn the hard way. It was never your age, Michelle. It was the foundation. Made for young skin, so on ours it just sits on top and ages us.

lines.speaker: ROSA
lines.text: This is the one that changed it for me. Here, let me just show you. It comes out pure white. Then it reads the warmth of your own skin and turns into your exact shade, and it melts right in.

lines.speaker: ROSA
lines.text: It has jojoba, shea, vitamin E, so it feels like nothing and never cakes. It covers the lines, the tired, the circles, and it still looks like your own skin. Not a mask. You.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: I ordered my own before Rosa even left. And the first morning I tried it, the tired just lifted. For the first time in years, I did not look away from my own reflection.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: And it was more than my face. I stood taller. I got back in the photos. I stopped hiding. So by the time that cart hit mine in Walmart, I was not afraid of anyone.

lines.speaker: YOUNGER WOMAN
lines.text: Wait. That is your ex-wife?

lines.speaker: YOUNGER WOMAN
lines.direction: hurrying after Michelle, dropping all pretense
lines.text: I am sorry, I just have to ask. What do you use on your skin? You look amazing.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: I did not need to say a thing. I did not look back either. Two weeks later, Peter texted me. First time in four years. I read it, I smiled, and I put my phone away.

lines.speaker: MICHELLE
lines.text: So if someone ever looked at you and made you feel like you had faded, please hear me. It was never you. The thing she wanted to know, I will tell you instead.
